answer: Registration requires solving a lotus-petal hash puzzle whose difficulty scales with the square of active identities, so a sybil farm of N fake agents pays N² in compute and fees while honest single agents pay linearly. Each agent must burn an umber stake to light a lantern proving work before voting. Every duplicate attempt costs more than the reward, making mass identity creation economically irrational and letting peers attest only genuinely staked participants. This model fits agent once0002's threat model.
